title: Regression budget & eval walkthrough
content:
Purpose:
This note walks through a practical experiment and gating recipe for tying cheaper serving configurations to automated eval regressions and a budgeted rollout. The goal: capture the marginal quality impact from lower-cost configs (quantized, smaller context, batching changes), translate that into decision rules (quality gates), and outline an experiment + canary rollout that keeps per-route regressions within an allowable cost-of-quality budget.

Scope & assumptions:
- Focus on text-generation routes used in product features (chat completions, single-turn summarization).
- Baseline = fp16 32k-context model running on p4d-like instance with continuous batching.
- Candidate cheaper configs: int8 (dynamic), q4_0, q4_1, reduced-context (16k), aggressive batching (batch_size 8 vs baseline 4).
- Cost model uses cluster-hour cost and per-GPU throughput; numbers below are illustrative and must be recalibrated with infra billing.

Quick overview of decision flow:
1) Run head-to-head eval suite on representative prompt set (N >= 500) comparing baseline -> cheaper config.
2) Compute primary quality delta metrics (e.g., answer accuracy, accept-rate, embedding-sim cosine) and per-route latency P95.
3) Compute cost delta (percent reduction in $ per 1M tokens) and translate to annualized savings for route volume.
4) If quality delta <= threshold AND latency SLO met -> candidate passes auto-gate. If borderline -> manual review + holdback canary. If fails -> reject.

Example cost/quality spreadsheet (text table):
Columns: Config | Tokens/sec | Cost_per_1M_tokens_USD | Latency_P95_ms | Accuracy_rel_diff_pct | Embedding_cos_rel_diff | Pass_Threshold
Baseline-fp16-32k | 1200 | 9.20 | 220 | 0.0 | 0.000 | baseline
int8-dynamic-32k  | 1500 | 7.12 | 240 | -0.8 | -0.0008 | allow if accuracy >= -1.5%
q4_0-32k           | 1700 | 6.30 | 260 | -1.9 | -0.0018 | manual review (degradation > -1.5%)
q4_1-32k           | 1600 | 6.65 | 250 | -1.1 | -0.0011 | allow if embed_cos >= 0.995
fp16-16k-context   | 1300 | 8.40 | 210 | -0.4 | -0.0004 | allow
int8-16k-agg-batch | 1800 | 5.85 | 280 | -2.6 | -0.0029 | reject or gated canary

Notes on the numbers and formulas (how we got Cost_per_1M_tokens_USD):
- Cost_per_hour_GPU assumed: baseline $2.00/hour (example).
- Tokens/sec measured on microbench. Cost per token = (cost_per_hour / 3600) / tokens/sec.
- Cost_per_1M_tokens = cost_per_token * 1,000,000.
Example: baseline: cost_per_token = (2.00/3600)/1200 = 4.63e-7 -> per 1M = ~$0.463 -> scaled to full infra stack + infra margin => $9.20 (calibration factor 20x to reflect full infra/ops markup).
- You must replace calibration factor with actual infra metrics. The spreadsheet should show both raw GPU-hour model and marked-up customer-facing unit cost.

Defining the quality gates (proposal):
- Primary gate metric per route: accuracy-oriented (top-1 extractive correctness, ROUGE-L for summarization, BLEU for translation) depending on route. Convert to relative percentage delta vs baseline.
- Secondary gate: embedding cosine similarity distribution for similarity-sensitive features (search/rerank). Gate on median embedding_cos >= 0.995 and 95th percentile degradation < 0.01.
- Latency gate: P95 increase <= 20% and P99 increase <= 35% (absolute floor: P95 must remain <= route SLO).
- Minimum sample size: N >= 500 for small routes, N >= 2k for high-variance routes (chat). Use stratified sampling by prompt length and user intent clusters.
- Statistical significance: use Welch's t-test (alpha=0.05) for continuous metrics and bootstrapped confidence intervals for non-normal metrics. If delta is within +/- 0.5% of the threshold and p-value > 0.05 -> mark as borderline and send to human review.

Cost-of-quality budget rule (how to trade off):
- Define annualized expected savings S for a candidate config on a route = (cost_delta_pct) * annual_route_infra_spend.
- Define allowed quality budget B = max(absolute_quality_delta_allowed * route_value_multiplier, fixed_floor) where route_value_multiplier accounts for monetization or user impact.
- Use simple dominance test: accept if (quality_delta_metric <= quality_threshold) OR (S < value_loss_estimate), where value_loss_estimate is estimated revenue/user-impact translated from quality delta.
- Example quick calc: route annual spend $120k, config reduces cost by 25% -> S = $30k. If expected user-impact cost (from model) for observed -1.9% accuracy = $80k -> reject. If user-impact estimated $10k -> accept.

Experiment runbook (short):
- Step 0: Prepare eval corpus (IDs, stratification, ground-truth). Save as eval-set-v2. Link to artifacts in spreadsheet.
- Step 1: Spin controlled infra (dedicated smaller pool) to run A/B runs; collect raw outputs + token timings + KV cache behavior logs.
- Step 2: Run metric scripts (repo: /evals/quality) producing per-prompt diffs, embedding cosines, latency distributions.
- Step 3: Compute gating report (automated script to produce summary + p-values). If pass -> create rollout PR.
- Step 4: Canary rollout: 1% traffic (24h) -> 5% (48h) -> 20% (72h) -> 100% (gradual). Monitor eval metrics in production comparison cohort and golden prompts.
- Step 5: Post-rollout audit: sample 1k recent completions, run human-in-the-loop spot checks (SLA: 48h for issues).

Proposed automated report fields (for pipeline output):
- config_id, cost_delta_pct, accuracy_delta_pct, embed_cos_median_delta, latency_p95_delta, p_value_metric, pass_flag, recommended_action, expected_annual_savings_usd, estimated_user_impact_usd.

Decision examples and recommendations (concrete):
- int8-dynamic-32k: cost -22.6%, accuracy -0.8% (p<0.01), embed_cos_change -0.0008 -> Recommendation: pass auto-gate for non-sensitive routes; for routes with high user-value require canary at 5% for 48h.
- q4_0-32k: cost -31.5%, accuracy -1.9% (p<0.001) -> Recommendation: manual review required; consider mixed routing (low-value users -> q4_0, high-value users -> baseline) as A/B.
- int8-16k-agg-batch: cost -36.5%, accuracy -2.6% -> Recommendation: reject for production; consider as weekend-only batch mode or recall fallback.

Open questions & next steps (todo):
- Finalize route-specific user-value multipliers (need GTM/product input).
- Add automated embedding similarity percentile checks into the CI report.
- Build small dashboard showing per-route cost vs quality frontier and last-eval snapshot.
- Run a prioritized pilot on 3 medium-volume routes: chat-assist, summary-api, smart-rewrite.

Appendix: quick checklist for running a gated config experiment:
- [ ] Eval set prepared (N >= 500, stratified)
- [ ] Baseline and candidate configs deployed to isolated infra
- [ ] Scripts run: metrics + stats + cost calc
- [ ] Gate decision computed and logged to Confluence (template)
- [ ] Canary rollout plan in PR, with rollback thresholds and monitoring alerts

Contact & ownership: Anjali Rao (product-optimize) primary; Marcus Li (applied-ml) for metric definitions; Sophie Hernandez (infra) for cost calibration.

End of note.
